findings: Every dsp-* fixture kind — dsp-binaural-{front,right,mirror,elevation,move,gain}, dsp-delay, dsp-convolver at 44100 and 48000 — passes on all three engines. The TuneJS DSP path is engine-independent for these workloads.

The only failure is the raw-host DelayNode reference row delayonly@48000 on Safari and Chrome-Android, with the byte-identical arithmeticError 1.0728836059570312e-05 (onset one frame early, 479 vs 480) — a shared non-Gecko rounding behavior in the host DelayNode, not a TuneJS defect. TuneJS delay() runs through the owned DSP path on browsers, so the engine is unaffected; the row remains as the host-limitation reference, same role as the native raw rows.
Firefox is the first host to pass all 38 rows including delayonly@48000.

Safari live probes are unmeasured, not failed: AudioContext.resume() pends without a user gesture and this session lacks automation permission; the live.html tab is left open at http://127.0.0.1:4174/live.html — one manual click completes the run (server: artifacts/host-matrix/serve4174.mjs on port 4174).
Android Chrome needed two command-line flags before the pages would run (first-run activity + autoplay); both are emulator-environment issues, recorded in NOTES.md.
